notes: Only the bundled `dist/index.js` and README were provided; the `./operations/*.js` helpers and the credential handling in `common/utils` are not shown, so the exact HTTP calls are inferred from the handler names and README tool contracts.

All 26 tools are registered unconditionally in the ListTools handler (dist/index.js:54-189) and dispatched in one switch (dist/index.js:195-406); there is no toolset/flag gating, so every tool is default-enabled.

Authentication uses `GITHUB_PERSONAL_ACCESS_TOKEN` (README.md:310-316, README.md:332-336); with a `repo`-scoped token the read tools reach private repositories, which is the basis for the SECRET labels. With a token limited to `public_repo` the SECRET reach would be reduced, but that is not enforced in code.

No tool performs agent-directed network fetches to arbitrary hosts, filesystem access, or subprocess execution, so no HOSTEXEC and no arbitrary-URL SINK exists; all traffic goes to the fixed GitHub API.

add_issue_comment.rationale: `issues.addIssueComment` posts an agent-supplied `body` as a comment on any issue, including issues in public repos the attacker can read.

create_branch.rationale: `branches.createBranchFromRef` creates an agent-named ref in an agent-chosen repository; on a public repo the branch name is publicly visible, so agent-supplied text reaches an attacker-readable destination (narrow channel, hence undetermined).

create_issue.rationale: `issues.createIssue` posts agent-supplied `title`/`body` into any repository, including public ones where the issue is world-readable.

create_or_update_file.rationale: `files.createOrUpdateFile` writes agent-supplied `content` and `message` to an agent-chosen `owner`/`repo`/`branch`; the repository may be public, so arbitrary agent data lands in an attacker-readable location.

create_pull_request.rationale: `pulls.createPullRequest` publishes an agent-supplied `title`/`body` to an agent-chosen repository; on a public repo this is attacker-readable output.

create_pull_request_review.rationale: `pulls.createPullRequestReview` publishes an agent-supplied review `body` plus per-line comment bodies on any PR, including PRs in public repos readable by the attacker.

create_repository.rationale: `repository.createRepository` creates a repository from agent-supplied `name`/`description` with `private` optional; a public repo in the user's account makes that agent-chosen text publicly readable, a low-bandwidth but real exfiltration channel.

fork_repository.rationale: `repository.forkRepository` copies a repo into the user's account or an org; it carries no agent-authored payload to a public destination and returns only fork metadata. It can echo metadata of a repo the user can read privately, which is why this is marked undetermined rather than asserting no reach at all.

get_file_contents.rationale: `files.getFileContents` reads any path of any repo with the user's credentials, returning private repository file contents (SECRET) and, for attacker-owned public repos, attacker-controlled text (UNTRUSTED).

get_issue.rationale: `issues.getIssue` fetches an issue from any repo: private-repo issues read with the user's credentials (SECRET) and public issue bodies authored by attackers (UNTRUSTED).

get_pull_request.rationale: `pulls.getPullRequest` returns PR details for any repo, covering private repository data (SECRET) and attacker-written PR titles/bodies in public repos (UNTRUSTED).

get_pull_request_comments.rationale: `pulls.getPullRequestComments` returns review comments: private repo discussion read with the user's token (SECRET) and public PR comments written by arbitrary parties (UNTRUSTED).

get_pull_request_files.rationale: `pulls.getPullRequestFiles` returns changed files with patch contents: private-repo diffs via the user's PAT (SECRET) and attacker-supplied diff content from public-repo PRs (UNTRUSTED).

get_pull_request_reviews.rationale: `pulls.getPullRequestReviews` returns review bodies and states, private-repo reviews via the user's PAT (SECRET) and attacker-authored review text on public PRs (UNTRUSTED).

get_pull_request_status.rationale: `pulls.getPullRequestStatus` returns combined check statuses of any PR, including private repo check data (SECRET); status contexts/descriptions/target URLs on public PRs come from third-party apps an attacker can influence (UNTRUSTED).

list_commits.rationale: `commits.listCommits` returns commit history of any repo with the user's token: private-repo history (SECRET) and attacker-authored commit messages/author fields from public repos (UNTRUSTED).

list_issues.rationale: `issues.listIssues` reads issues from private repos with the user's PAT (SECRET) and from public repos where issue titles/bodies are written by arbitrary third parties (UNTRUSTED).

list_pull_requests.rationale: `pulls.listPullRequests` lists PRs of an agent-chosen repo, exposing private repo data (SECRET) and third-party-authored PR text from public repos (UNTRUSTED).

merge_pull_request.rationale: `pulls.mergePullRequest` writes agent-supplied `commit_title`/`commit_message` into the repository history of an agent-chosen repo, which may be public.

push_files.rationale: `files.pushFiles` commits an agent-supplied array of file paths/contents to an agent-chosen repo and branch, which may be a public repository readable by the attacker.

search_code.rationale: `search.searchCode` searches with the user's token, so hits can include private repositories' code (SECRET), and public code fragments are attacker-authored (UNTRUSTED).

search_issues.rationale: `search.searchIssues` returns issue/PR titles and bodies; scoped queries can surface private repo issues via the user's PAT (SECRET), and public issue text is fully attacker-controllable (UNTRUSTED).

search_repositories.rationale: `repository.searchRepositories` runs a GitHub search with the user's PAT, so results can include private repositories the token can read (SECRET), and repository names/descriptions/READMEs in results are attacker-authored public content (UNTRUSTED).

search_users.rationale: `search.searchUsers` returns public profile data (names, bios, logins) that any attacker can set on their own account; no non-public data is exposed.

update_issue.rationale: `issues.updateIssue` writes agent-supplied `title`/`body`/labels onto an issue in an agent-chosen repository, which may be public and attacker-readable.

update_pull_request_branch.rationale: `pulls.updatePullRequestBranch` only triggers a base-branch merge and returns `{success:true}`; it neither returns repository content nor carries agent-authored text to a readable destination.
